title: Prompt provenance & edit-lineage idea log
content:
Purpose / problem statement:

- Users build prompts iteratively (copy/paste, tweak, fork). When an app surface shows unexpected output or regressions we currently lack an obvious record of which prompt variant produced it, who edited it, or why changes were made.
- Need lightweight prompt provenance (who/when/why), an edit-lineage UI, and a server-side signal that operators and customers can use for debugging, evals, and compliance (audit).

Goals (high level):
- Capture minimal metadata for each prompt invocation (prompt-id, prompt-version, author-hash, env tags, model & model-config).
- Surface a compact edit history in the Console and optionally include it in API responses for debugging-only tokens (opt-in).
- Support privacy constraints: strip PII from provenance summaries; configurable retention & redaction.
- Keep runtime overhead tiny: most tracing should be metadata-only (no prompt body retention by default).

Primary user stories:
- SRE: "When latency/regression spikes for customer X, I want to know which prompt template version they used, and the recent edits or rollouts applied, so I can correlate with model rollouts."
- Product engineer: "I pushed a tweak to the billing assistant prompt yesterday. A customer reports hallucination; I want to quickly replay the exact prompt-version (and see diffs) to reproduce locally."
- Compliance officer: "For an audit we need a tamper-evident record of prompt changes and who approved them for the production flow."
- Customer developer: "I want a stable prompt identifier so I can pin my integration to a specific prompt revision and avoid silent behavior changes."

MVP scope (opinionated):
- 1) Prompt ID & version token: a short stable identifier assigned at authoring time (uuid v4 truncated) and incrementing semantic version (auto bump on author edits).
- 2) Store metadata per version: author (name/email), timestamp, short commit message, model pin, config fingerprint (quant/beam/batch), enabled flag.
- 3) Console UI: lightweight timeline view showing versions for a prompt template with in-line diff (text diff of last two versions).
- 4) API: optional header X-Redwood-Prompt-Version returned when you pass ?include_provenance=true (developer-only, no PII).
- 5) Retention policy: by default keep metadata 90 days; allow enterprise to configure longer retention and full prompt-body retention behind contract/KMS.

Stretch / future:
- Signed provenance bundles (for audit) — exportable ZIP containing versions + tamper-evident signature.
- Integration with evals: tie prompt versions to evaluation runs automatically.
- Fine-grained redaction rules (regex policies) and automated PII scrubbers for prompt bodies.

Technical considerations / constraints:
- Storage: metadata small; can live in existing config store (feature-flags DB) but need query endpoints optimized for Console listing.
- Runtime performance: do not attach full prompt body to every inference request; instead attach prompt-version token. If customer opts-in for full capture, write prompt body to an encrypted blob store async.
- Uniqueness: prompt-version tokens should be stable across exports and visible in logs so SRE can grep.
- Backwards compat: default behavior must be opt-in for hosted customers to avoid surprising telemetry.

Console UX sketch (notes):
- Prompt editor sidebar: "Versions" panel with compact cards: version number | author | short msg | time | model pin | diff toggle.
- Quick actions: revert-to-version, create-branch (creates a forked prompt id for experimentation), export provenance bundle.
- View-mode exposes only metadata; full prompt text shown only if user has "prompt-view" permission.

API sketch (example):
- POST /v1/generate with body {"prompt_template_id": "pt-123", "prompt_version": "v3"} -> Response contains header X-Redwood-Prompt-Version: "pt-123:v3" when include_provenance=true.
- GET /v1/prompt-templates/pt-123/versions -> returns list of version metadata (no bodies unless authorized + capture enabled).

Security & privacy:
- Default: only metadata stored (no bodies). Bodies stored only when customer elects + encrypted at rest + access gated by IAM and audit logs.
- Redaction: add a pipeline stage that can optionally redact user PII from captured bodies (PII regex + ML-based detector).
- Access controls: Console actions guarded by RBAC (author, admin roles).

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve in next sync):
- Should prompt-version tokens be globally unique or namespaced by customer? (namespacing prevents collisions but complicates logs).
- How to represent ephemeral prompts created client-side (ad-hoc, no template ID)? Assign ephemeral IDs with TTL?
- Opt-in vs opt-out: for debugging we could offer ephemeral provenance cookies per signed session; does that create compliance exposure?
- UI/UX friction: will extra provenance UI overwhelm users who just want a simple editor? Consider collapsible default.

Implementation plan (first 3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: Schema design for prompt-version metadata, backend store prototype, minimal API to create/bump versions.
- Sprint 2: Console versions panel prototype + basic diff rendering; unit tests for metadata retention.
- Sprint 3: API header wiring, gated feature flag rollout to internal customers, simple docs + example for debugging workflows.

Risks:
- Customer privacy backlash if bodies are captured by default; mitigate via opt-in and clear docs.
- Storage costs if many customers opt into full capture; mitigate with economic tiering and retention defaults.
- Developer confusion around version semantics; require clear UX microcopy and predictable auto-versioning rules.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Sync with Legal on retention & export requirements (Jill from legal).
- Draft Confluence spec with data model and API samples (owner: me, due EOW).
- Quick prototype in Console: wire up fake data to show version cards (ask Maya to abridge design resources).
- Add JIRA epic and sub-tasks: JIRA-REPRO-891 is placeholder; create concrete tickets for backend, console, SDKs.

Notes to self: keep feature minimal and privacy-first; provenance is powerful for debugging but a liability if mis-handled. Aim for a tiny, opt-in, auditable footprint for MVP.

----
Backup links & references (internal):
- Slack thread: #prod-prompt-provenance (ref: thread 4567)
- Related ideas: developer-replay-workbench-prd-seeds.json (local replay UX)
- Inspiration: "git for prompts" discussions with platform-eng (Oct 2024)

Fragmented brainstorm points left here (freeform):
- Could we hash prompt body and surface only hash by default; fetch body only if dev clicks "show" and has permission? low friction.
- Branching model: name branches with semantic tags (canary, stable, experiment).
- Use case: automated rollback when a prompt-version correlates with quality regression across customers (tie into Rollouts).

End of notes.
